key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Sudden onset over hours. LOCATION: Systemic, respiratory. DURATION: 3-7 days, can last longer. CHARACTER: High fever, severe body aches, dry cough. AGGRAVATING: Exertion, cold air. RELIEVING: Rest, fluids, antipyretics. TIMING: Acute, seasonal. SEVERITY: Moderate to severe (6-8/10). ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: High fever, chills, severe body aches, headache, dry cough, sore throat, fatigue, weakness. KEY POSITIVES: High fever, body aches, dry cough, seasonal. KEY NEGATIVES: No chest pain (unless secondary), no wheezing (unless reactive airway disease).

red_flags: Severe weakness or inability to move
